library(powerjoin)
library(skimr)
library(visdat)
library(ggpubr)
library(rsample)
library(recipes)
library(workflows)
library(workflowsets)
library(tune)
library(yardstick)
library(parsnip)
library(dials)

root  <- 'https://gdex.ucar.edu/dataset/camels/file'
types <- c("clim", "geol", "soil", "topo", "vege", "hydro")

remote_files <- glue::glue('{root}/camels_{types}.txt')
local_files  <- glue::glue('data/camels_{types}.txt')

walk2(remote_files, local_files, download.file, quiet = TRUE)

camels_list <- map(local_files, read_delim, show_col_types = FALSE)

camels <- reduce(camels_list, power_full_join, by = "gauge_id")
camels_clean <- camels %>%
  filter(!is.na(gauge_lat) & !is.na(gauge_lon)) %>%
  distinct()

camels_clean <- camels_clean %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

skim(camels_clean)

linear_model <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
rf_model <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) %>%
  set_engine("ranger") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
xgb_model <- boost_tree(trees = 500, learn_rate = tune(), mtry = tune(), tree_depth = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
camels_train <- camels_train %>%
  filter(!is.na(q_mean), !is.infinite(q_mean))

set.seed(123)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(camels_train, v = 10)

camels_recipe <- recipe(q_mean ~ ., data = camels_train) %>%
  step_rm(gauge_id, gauge_lat, gauge_lon) %>%         
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%  
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%                       
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
model_list <- list(
  linear = linear_model,
  xgb    = xgb_model   
)

model_workflows <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(camels_recipe),
  models = model_list
)

set.seed(123)
model_results <- model_workflows %>%
  workflow_map("tune_grid", resamples = cv_folds, grid = 3, metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq))

Based on the RMSE and R-squared metrics, the linear regression model performed the best. It had the lowest RMSE, which means it made the most accurate predictions on average, and the highest R-squared, indicating it explained the most variance in the outcome (q_mean). Also, the performance was very consistent across cross-validation folds.

The selected model is a linear regression model, using the lm engine in regression mode. It probably did well because the relationship between the predictors and streamflow (q_mean) may be mostly linear, or because linear models generalize well when the data is clean, high-quality, and not overly complex. The simplicity of the model helps prevent overfitting and makes the results easier to interpret.

Model Tuning

rf_model <- rand_forest(
  trees = tune(),   
  mtry = tune(),    
  min_n = tune()    
) %>%
  set_engine("ranger") %>%
  set_mode("regression")  

rf_grid <- grid_regular(
  trees(range = c(100, 500)),  
  mtry(range = c(1, 10)),      
  min_n(range = c(2, 10)),     
  levels = 3                   
)

recipe <- recipe(q_mean ~ ., data = camels_train)

rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_model) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

cv_folds <- vfold_cv(camels_train, v = 10)

tuned_rf <- rf_workflow %>%
  tune_grid(
    resamples = cv_folds,   
    grid = rf_grid,         
    metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq)  
  )
xgb_tuned <- boost_tree(
  trees = 500,                  
  learn_rate = tune(),          
  mtry = tune(),                
  tree_depth = tune()           
) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
wf_tune <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(xgb_tuned) %>%
  add_recipe(camels_recipe)
dials <- extract_parameter_set_dials(wf_tune)
dials <- finalize(dials, camels_train)

my.grid <- grid_space_filling(dials, size = 25)

camels_recipe <- recipe(q_mean ~ ., data = camels_train) %>%
  step_rm(gauge_id, gauge_lat, gauge_lon,
          geol_2nd_class, geol_porostiy, root_depth_50, root_depth_99) %>%         
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%  
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%                       
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
wf_tune <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(xgb_tuned) %>%
  add_recipe(camels_recipe)

wf_final <- finalize_workflow(wf_tune, hp_best)

final_model <- last_fit(wf_final, split = split)

collect_metrics(final_model)

final_predictions <- collect_predictions(final_model)
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(final_predictions, aes(x = .pred, y = q_mean)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#1f77b4") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Final XGBoost Predictions vs Actual q_mean",
    x = "Predicted q_mean",
    y = "Actual q_mean"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
final_fit <- fit(wf_final, data = camels_all)

augmented <- augment(final_fit, new_data = camels_all)

augmented <- augmented %>%
  mutate(residual = (q_mean - .pred)^2)
p1 <- ggplot(augmented, aes(x = gauge_lon, y = gauge_lat, color = .pred)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Predicted q_mean Across Sites") +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  coord_fixed()

p2 <- ggplot(augmented, aes(x = gauge_lon, y = gauge_lat, color = residual)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Residuals (Squared Error)") +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  coord_fixed()

library(patchwork)
p1 + p2
ggsave("q_mean_predictions_map.png", p1 + p2, width = 10, height = 5)
